title: The 3-Paycheck Months of 2027 (and What to Do With Them)

lines.say: Twenty twenty-seven starts on a Friday.
And if you're paid every other Friday, that could mean an extra paycheck.

lines.cap: A year that starts on a Friday has 53 Fridays. So one every-other-Friday schedule gets 27 paychecks instead of 26.
lines.say: A year that starts on a Friday has fifty-three Fridays. So one of the two every-other-Friday schedules gets twenty-seven paychecks, instead of twenty-six.
And everyone paid every two weeks gets at least two months with three paychecks. Here's exactly which months, and what to do with them.
Step one. Find your months.

scene.head: Schedule A · every other Friday from Jan 1
scene.foot: Jan 1 check paid Dec 31? Then your months are July & December.

lines.cap: If your paydays fall on January 1, 15 and 29, you're on schedule A.
lines.say: If your paydays fall on January first, fifteenth, and twenty-ninth, you're on schedule A.

lines.cap: Your 3-paycheck months: January, July and December. 27 paychecks in all.
lines.say: Your three-paycheck months are January, July, and December. Twenty-seven paychecks in all.

lines.cap: One catch: January 1 is a holiday, so many employers pay on December 31 instead. Then that check counts toward 2026, and your extra months are July and December.
lines.say: One catch. January first is a holiday, so many employers pay on December thirty-first instead. Then that check counts toward twenty twenty-six, and your extra months are July and December.

scene.head: Schedule B · every other Friday from Jan 8

lines.cap: If your first paydays are January 8 and 22, you're on schedule B.
lines.say: If your first paydays are January eighth and twenty-second, you're on schedule B.

lines.cap: Your 3-paycheck months: April and October. 26 paychecks.
lines.say: Your three-paycheck months are April and October. Twenty-six paychecks.
Paid on another weekday? Your months shift a little. The planner at the end finds yours.

scene.text: Paid every two weeks? This one's for you.

lines.cap: Paid twice a month, like the 15th and the last day? You get exactly 24 paychecks, never a third in one month. This one's for every-two-weeks people.
lines.say: And if you're paid twice a month, like on the fifteenth and the last day, you get exactly twenty-four paychecks, and never a third in one month. This one's for every-two-weeks people.
Step two. Understand why the third check is different.

scene.label: The third paycheck of the month
scene.sub: has no bills attached. They're covered by checks 1 and 2.

lines.say: If you budget by paycheck like we did in episode one, your bills are already covered by the first two checks of the month.

lines.cap: So the third check, $1,850 in our example, has nothing attached to it. Which is exactly why it tends to disappear.
lines.say: So the third check, eighteen fifty in our example, has nothing attached to it. Which is exactly why it tends to disappear.
Step three. Give it a job before it lands.

scene.head: One way to split an extra $1,850

lines.say: Here's one way to split it.
A thousand to your debt target.
Five hundred to your emergency fund.
A hundred sixty-five to sinking funds.

lines.cap: And about 10%, $185, for something fun. You earned it.
lines.say: And about ten percent, one eighty-five, for something fun. You earned it.

scene.label: Extra paychecks in 2027
scene.sub: two extra checks, or $5,550 with three

lines.cap: Two extra checks is $3,700 this year. On schedule A, with three, it's $5,550.
lines.say: Two extra checks is thirty-seven hundred dollars this year. On schedule A, with three, it's fifty-five fifty.
That's a whole credit card paid off, or a real emergency fund, from money you were never budgeting for anyway.

scene.text: Put the dates in your calendar today.

lines.say: So, put the dates in your calendar today, and decide the split now, while it's easy.
Then set up the transfers ahead of time, so the money moves on payday, before it can disappear.
